title: /ai-evidence/* route tree is blocked without the evidence.read permission
description: Regression guard for CP-1 (2026-07-22): layout.jsx previously had zero permission gating anywhere under /ai-evidence — upload, delete, and accept/reject actions were visible to any authenticated user regardless of permissions. layout.jsx now wraps the tree in PermissionGate permission='evidence.read' allowProjectGrant.
preconditions: A user account with zero evidence.* permissions and no project-level grant
steps: Log in as the unprivileged user
expectedResult: Both routes are blocked by PermissionGate (redirect or access-denied state) — no upload UI, evidence data, or AI suggestions render.

title: POST /api/evidence/upload/ai rejects an executable disguised with an allowed extension via magic-byte sniffing
description: validateMagicBytes (evidence-upload.multer.js) reads the first 4100 bytes via the file-type package and rejects binaries whose detected MIME isn't in ALLOWED_DETECTED_MIMES, independent of the declared/extension MIME.
steps: Attempt to upload a Windows PE executable renamed to 'certificate.pdf' via /api/evidence/upload/ai
expectedResult: Upload is rejected with 400 and message "File 'certificate.pdf' contains disallowed content (detected type: application/x-msdownload)" or equivalent — no evidence document or AI extraction call is made.

title: Review page's GET /api/evidence/:evidenceId rejects an AI-assisted draft ID belonging to another organization
preconditions: Two orgs (A, B), org B has an AI-assisted draft in status 'draft'
Valid JWT for a user in org A with evidence.read
steps: As an org A user, call GET /api/evidence/:evidenceId using org B's draft evidenceId (e.g. by navigating to /ai-evidence/:evidenceId/review with a guessed/enumerated ID)
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403/404 — no title, AI suggestions, or file metadata belonging to org B is returned.

title: extract-metadata-fast ignores organization_id/project_id for classification scope — verify results are identical regardless of tenant, confirming no unintended cross-tenant document leakage exists
description: python-notebookAI-service/routers/documents.py requires organization_id/project_id as query params on /api/v1/documents/extract-metadata-fast and logs them, but never uses them to scope the classification — category/subcategory embeddings are shared global master taxonomy, not tenant data, loaded into a process-wide in-memory cache. This test exists to positively confirm the classification path never reaches into a tenant-specific document index or another org's indexed evidence (the risk this test guards is a future regression where someone wires tenant-scoped RAG/document lookup into this endpoint without adding org filtering).
preconditions: Org A and Org B each have their own indexed evidence/documents from prior uploads
steps: Submit the same file content for AI extraction once with organization_id=orgA/project_id=projA, and once with organization_id=orgB/project_id=projB
Compare the two extracted_metadata responses (title, summary, category/subcategory suggestions, confidence scores)
expectedResult: Both calls return equivalent classification results driven only by the shared master taxonomy — no field in either response contains content, titles, or references traceable to the other org's previously indexed documents.

title: Presigned download URL for AI-assisted evidence forces Content-Disposition: attachment and Content-Type: application/octet-stream regardless of the file's real type
description: getPresignedUrl (s3-file-storage.js) always overrides response headers to force a download rather than inline rendering, specifically to prevent stored XSS from an uploaded HTML/SVG file being rendered in-browser under the evidence viewer.
preconditions: An AI-assisted evidence item has a file that passed upload validation as text/plain or text/csv
steps: Request the file download URL for the AI-assisted evidence item
Inspect the actual HTTP response headers returned when fetching the presigned URL
expectedResult: Content-Disposition is 'attachment; filename=...' and Content-Type is 'application/octet-stream' regardless of the stored file's real MIME type — the browser is never able to render the file inline.

title: AI-assisted upload endpoint enforces a 20-requests-per-15-minutes-per-IP rate limit
steps: From a single IP, issue 21 rapid POST requests to /api/evidence/upload/ai within a 15-minute window
expectedResult: The 21st request is rejected with 429 and message 'Too many uploads from this IP, please try again later.'

title: An HTML file with a spoofed .pdf extension is still blocked by the MIME allowlist layer even though text-based content bypasses magic-byte binary sniffing
description: validateMagicBytes lets text-based formats through unexamined because file-type returns null for them ('cannot be PE/ELF binaries'), relying entirely on the upstream Multer fileFilter MIME allowlist (which excludes text/html) to catch this case. Confirms the two layers together still close the gap.
steps: Upload a file named 'invoice.pdf' whose actual content is '<script>alert(1)</script>' HTML, sent with Content-Type: application/pdf declared but real bytes being HTML
expectedResult: Upload is rejected — either at the Multer fileFilter MIME-declaration layer or by explicit content sniffing; the file is never persisted or surfaced for inline rendering.
